name: Halftime Over/Under (SVM)
summary: Set the halftime numbers and any total you like, and a support vector machine says which side of its over/under boundary the game is on.

card.holdout_label: 2025 season onward (422 games the model never saw)
card.metric_note: Two tests, both on seasons the model never saw. 'Pregame total' asks the old question: will the game clear its pregame over/under? 'Spread of totals' asks about seven different totals per game, from 10.5 points under to 10.5 over a rough pace guess, which is closer to how you will use the page. Accuracy is the share of calls that were right at a 50% cutoff. Log loss scores the percentages themselves and punishes confident misses; lower is better and always saying 50% scores 0.693. AUC measures how well the percentages rank games (0.5 is a coin flip, 1.0 is perfect).
card.threshold_note: Measured on 36,174 game-and-total pairs the model had not seen when it scored them (cross-validation folds plus the test seasons).

sections.title: How the settings were chosen
paragraphs: An SVM has three settings to pick before training. The kernel is the shape the boundary may take: a straight line (linear) or a curve (RBF). C is how hard it tries to get every training row on the right side: high C bends to fit individual games, low C keeps the boundary simple. Gamma, for the curved kernel, is how far one game's influence reaches: high gamma makes a wiggly local boundary, low gamma a smooth one.

A grid search scored all 23 combinations with six rounds of cross-validation, each round training on earlier seasons and grading on later ones. Best log loss was 0.4395; the worst combination scored 0.4638.
sections.note: Top 8 combinations. The first row is the model on this page. These scores use random totals, so they are not comparable with the test table above.

findings: An SVM draws one boundary between game-and-total pairs that went over and pairs that stayed under, then reports which side you are on and how far from the line. The total you want to test is one of its inputs. The grid search picked a curved boundary (RBF kernel, gamma 0.01) with C = 3.

Points still needed decides most calls: how far your total is above what is already on the board. Shuffling it wrecks the model. The pregame over/under is a distant second, and the other inputs add slivers.

Curved or straight barely matters. The best straight-line boundary scored 0.4408 in cross-validation and the best curved one 0.4395. The real boundary is close to a straight line, which is why the plain linear model keeps up.

6,805 of the 14,614 training rows ended up as support vectors, the rows close enough to the boundary to shape it. That is 47% of them, which says overs and unders overlap heavily at halftime: there is no clean gap to find.

Honest scorecard on seasons it never saw. On the pregame total, the SVM was right 73.7% of the time, against 75.4% for the linear model on this site and 74.2% for the simple pace rule. Across a spread of totals it was right 73.1% of the time (linear 73.7%), with log loss 0.540 against 0.540 (lower is better). Too close to separate on a test this size, so call it a tie.
limitations: It only knows what you enter. Injuries, a quarterback change or weather that turns at halftime are invisible to it.

There are no real halftime betting lines in the training data. The model learned from every game paired with made-up totals near a normal pace, so it answers 'how often do games like this clear that number', not 'is the live line wrong'.
A whole-number total can land exactly on the final score (a push). Those cases were left out, so the two sides always add up to 100%.
Sliders move independently, so you can enter combinations that rarely happen in real games. Unusual inputs are flagged.
An SVM does not produce percentages on its own. The chance shown comes from a second small model fit on top of it, which adds its own error.
It is the hardest of these models to explain: there are no coefficients or trees to read, only a boundary in six dimensions.
card.disclaimer: For information and learning only. Not betting advice.
